title: SatQuery AI - An Interactive Vision-Language Assistant for Multimodal Remote Sensing Image Analysis through Text Queries
department: Department of Space / Indian Space Research Organisation
dataset_link:
Training / Fine-Tuning Dataset BigEarthNet.txt - primary dataset for remote-sensing adaptation using co-registered Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery, and diverse text annotations. Link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.29630. All datasets are available online open source.

Public Evaluation Benchmarks

• VRSBench - for r
description:
Background Remote-sensing imagery is widely used for agricultural monitoring, disaster management, urban planning, forest monitoring, water-resource assessment, infrastructure mapping, and environmental analysis. However, most existing remote-sensing AI solutions are developed as isolated applications for a single predefined task, such as land-cover classification, object detection, visual question answering, or change detection. These systems often require users to understand satellite-data characteristics, GIS workflows, model selection, and task-specific parameters. Consequently, non-expert users may find it difficult to obtain meaningful information from satellite imagery through simple natural-language queries.
Many operational remote-sensing questions cannot always be answered reliably using a single optical image. Relevant information may be distributed across paired or multiple observations acquired at different times or by different sensors. Optical and multispectral imagery provides spectral and contextual information, whereas synthetic aperture radar (SAR) provides complementary structural information and supports day-and-night acquisition through cloud cover. Multitemporal image pairs are required to identify and interpret changes over time, while co-registered optical–SAR pairs can provide more complete and reliable information than either modality alone.
A general-purpose large language model (LLM) or vision-language model (VLM) cannot be expected to perform these specialised tasks reliably without adaptation to remote-sensing imagery, sensor characteristics, and domain-specific terminology. The proposed solution must therefore include remote-sensing fine-tuning or domain adaptation and may employ multiple specialised models for different tasks. BigEarthNet.txt will serve as the primary dataset for adapting image–text representations to multisensor remote-sensing data. VRSBench and RSVQA will be used to evaluate single-image captioning, grounding, and visual question answering, while CDVQA will be used to evaluate multitemporal change-based visual question answering.
The novelty of SatQuery AI lies in its agentic, query-driven framework. Instead of applying a single generic VLM, the system selects and executes suitable remote-sensing specialist models, validates inputs, combines their outputs, and returns an evidence-grounded response.
Description The objective is to develop SatQuery AI, a software-based agentic vision-language assistant for analysing single and paired remote-sensing images through natural-language queries. Single-image understanding is a mandatory baseline, while the principal focus is joint reasoning over paired cross-modal and multitemporal imagery.
Defined Input Scope
• Single image: One optical/multispectral or SAR image for captioning, visual question answering, and text-guided region grounding.
• Cross-modal pair: Co-registered optical/multispectral and SAR images of the same geographic area for joint information extraction and cross-modal analysis.
• Bi-temporal pair: Two spatially corresponding images of the same geographic area acquired at different times for change detection, change description, and change-based visual question answering.
• Supported formats: GeoTIFF or TIFF for geospatial imagery. PNG and JPEG inputs may be accepted only for the prescribed public benchmark datasets.
Mandatory Functional Scope
• Remote-sensing adaptation: At least one visual or vision-language component must be fine-tuned or otherwise adapted using BigEarthNet.txt or the any open source training data.
• Single-image baseline: Visual question answering shall be mandatory. Each solution must additionally implement either captioning/scene description or text-guided region grounding.
• Multi-image change analysis: Change description or change-based visual question answering from a bi-temporal image pair shall be mandatory. A spatial change map may also be generated where reference masks are available.
• Cross-modal pair analysis: The system must extract complementary information from a co-registered optical/multispectral and SAR image pair.
• Agentic orchestration: The system must automatically select, sequence, and execute the appropriate specialist models or tools according to the query and input configuration.
Representative Queries
• 'Describe the land-cover and major objects visible in this image.'
• 'Highlight the water body referred to in the query.'
• 'What changed between these two dates, and where did the change occur?'
• 'Use the optical and SAR images together to identify built-up and water-covered regions.'
• 'Has the built-up area increased, decreased, or remained unchanged?'
Agentic Model and Tool Orchestration The system may use multiple specialised components, such as a remote-sensing VQA or captioning model, a grounding model, a change-understanding or change-VQA model, and an optical–SAR fusion or information-extraction model.
• interpret the query and classify the requested task;
• check the number, modality, format, metadata, and compatibility of the input images;
• select one or more models or tools from a predefined registry;
• configure only permitted task parameters and execute the selected workflow;
• combine textual and spatial outputs, estimate confidence, and return visual evidence; and
• provide an auditable execution summary containing the selected task, model/tool names, and key parameters.
The controller may perform internal task planning; however, only the observable execution trace, including the selected task, models or tools, permitted parameters, and outputs will be evaluated. Internal reasoning text is neither required nor evaluated.
Expected Solution The expected solution is an interactive GUI or web application with an agentic remote-sensing AI backend. It should accept supported image inputs and natural-language queries, select the appropriate specialist workflow, and return evidence-grounded textual and visual results.
The solution should include:
• Input upload and compatibility checking.
• A remote-sensing-adapted vision-language component.
• Specialist tools for VQA, captioning or grounding, change understanding, and optical–SAR analysis.
• An agentic controller for task routing, tool execution, and output integration.
• Visual evidence, confidence information, execution summaries, and downloadable reports.
Each solution must demonstrate single-image VQA, one additional single-image task, multitemporal change understanding, optical–SAR paired-image analysis, and agentic model/tool orchestration. A generic LLM or VLM without remote-sensing adaptation will not satisfy the requirements.
Deliverables An interactive GUI or web application with an agentic remote-sensing AI backend, Codes and models including test and demonstration.
Implementation Scope The system shall support single optical/multispectral or SAR images, co-registered optical–SAR pairs, and bi-temporal pairs in GeoTIFF/TIFF or approved benchmark formats. It must perform single-image VQA, one additional single-image task, change analysis, optical–SAR joint analysis, and agentic model/tool selection through an interactive GUI or web application.
Evaluation/Judging Criteria Final evaluation will use prescribed public benchmark test subsets and an ISRO/SAC evaluation dataset. Scores will be normalised before combining different metrics.
Add 'Evaluation/Judging Criteria' table here Public benchmarks will be evaluated using the prescribed test splits. The ISRO/SAC evaluation set will contain pre-georeferenced and co-registered Cartosat-2S optical and RISAT SAR image pairs, with task-specific reference answers, labels, bounding boxes, or masks, as applicable. Evaluation annotations will not be disclosed to participating teams.
summary: Innovation (5/5): draws on ai, satellite, gis applied to a space technology problem, placing it in the breakthrough band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (3/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Space Technology. Tech Depth (5/5): centers on integration, sensor, gis. Sustainability (3/5): will need a maintenance/upkeep plan post-hackathon. Scalability (3/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 22/30 -> Green verdict.

detail.title: SatQuery AI - An Interactive Vision-Language Assistant for Multimodal Remote Sensing Image Analysis through Text Queries

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a vision-language AI that lets non-experts ask plain-language questions about satellite imagery, and get answers, combining information across multiple images and sensor types (optical and radar), without needing to understand GIS workflows or select the right specialized model themselves.
overview.why_it_matters: Most remote-sensing AI tools are isolated, single-task applications requiring GIS expertise. A genuine conversational interface makes satellite imagery analysis accessible to non-expert users across agriculture, disaster management, and more.
pain_points: Existing remote-sensing AI solutions are isolated, single-task applications requiring GIS expertise to use.
Non-expert users struggle to extract meaningful information from satellite imagery via natural language.
Many real questions need information distributed across multiple images/sensors (optical, SAR, multi-temporal), not a single image.
overview.background: Remote-sensing AI is typically single-task and GIS-expertise-dependent, but many operational questions need information combined across multiple images, sensor types, and time periods, motivating a conversational, multimodal vision-language assistant.
overview.whats_being_asked: An interactive vision-language assistant answering natural-language queries about remote-sensing imagery, combining information across multiple images and sensor modalities (optical, multispectral, SAR).
expected_solution: Natural language query understanding for remote-sensing questions.
Vision-language model grounding answers in actual image content.
Accessible for non-expert users without GIS workflow knowledge.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Very High. Genuine multimodal (optical + SAR), multi-image vision-language reasoning for remote sensing is active, cutting-edge research territory, real conceptual and technical sophistication.
analysis.invention_effort_note: High. Combining vision-language model architectures with genuine multi-sensor, multi-temporal reasoning is substantial technical depth, likely one of the more advanced ML PS in this batch.

competitive_landscape.note: Requires genuine vision-language model and remote-sensing expertise together, a narrow, technically demanding field.

innovation.note: Multi-sensor, multi-image vision-language reasoning for remote sensing is genuine, active research-territory innovation.

invention.note: Combining VLM architectures with genuine cross-sensor, cross-temporal reasoning represents substantial technical depth.

technical_feasibility.tag: Tight for Full Multimodal Reasoning, Comfortable for a Single-Modality Baseline
technical_feasibility.note: Full optical-plus-SAR combined reasoning in 36 hours is ambitious, scoping to strong single-image or single-modality VLM capability with multi-image extension as a stretch goal is more realistic.

impact_and_benefits.note: Genuinely valuable across agriculture, disaster management, urban planning if it lowers the barrier to remote-sensing analysis for non-experts.

architecture.note: Vision-language model integration with multi-source remote-sensing data handling, genuine architectural sophistication.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Strong pick, one of the higher-scoring PS in this batch, genuinely achievable if scoped to a strong core capability (single or same-modality multi-image VLM query answering) with multimodal (optical+SAR) reasoning as an ambitious stretch goal.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Very well-articulated, genuine research gap (existing tools are single-task and GIS-expertise-dependent) gives clear motivation and differentiation.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Attempting full optical-plus-SAR combined reasoning without a strong, validated single-modality foundation first would likely produce a shallow demo across both rather than a genuinely working core capability.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Build and validate strong single-image, natural-language query-answering capability first (using an existing vision-language model as a foundation, fine-tuned or prompted for remote-sensing imagery), then extend to multi-image/multi-sensor reasoning as time allows, rather than attempting full multimodal complexity from the start.

idea_0_4: Choose an existing vision-language model architecture as your foundation (open VLMs adaptable to remote sensing exist).
Source public remote-sensing imagery (optical, and SAR if attempting multimodal) for your test queries.
Split: one person on VLM integration/query handling, one on remote-sensing-specific adaptation and data preparation.
prototype_4_22: Build your core natural-language query-answering capability against single remote-sensing images.
Test with realistic remote-sensing questions (land-cover identification, change detection between two images of the same area).
Start multi-image reasoning (comparing two images of the same area at different times) as your first extension.
integration_22_30: Refine query-answering accuracy and groundedness (answers should reference actual image content, not hallucinate).
If time allows, extend to basic SAR imagery handling as a stretch goal.
Build the conversational interface connecting query input to grounded image-based answers.
polish_30_36: Polish the interface for genuine non-expert usability.
Rehearse a live demo asking realistic remote-sensing questions and getting accurate, grounded answers.
Prepare to discuss your scoping choice (single/multi-image versus full multimodal) honestly.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Ask a genuinely tricky remote-sensing question live that requires comparing two images of the same area (e.g. 'what changed here between these two dates'), and show your system correctly grounding its answer in actual image content, that multi-image reasoning capability, even without full SAR integration, is a strong, credible core demonstration.

strengths: Very well-articulated, genuine research gap gives clear motivation.
Existing vision-language model architectures provide a real foundation to adapt.
weaknesses: Full multimodal (optical+SAR) reasoning is genuinely ambitious for 36 hours, requires honest scoping.
Grounding VLM answers accurately in real image content (avoiding hallucination) is a real, non-trivial challenge.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: VLM-skill-weighted, with real remote-sensing domain grounding for accurate query handling.
team_fit.approach: Build and validate strong single-image query-answering first, this de-risks your core demo before attempting multimodal extension.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: The core VLM integration and conversational interface using existing model architectures.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Ensuring answers are genuinely grounded in real image content and correctly account for remote-sensing-specific interpretation challenges (sensor characteristics, spectral bands), that requires real domain understanding.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: An ungrounded VLM could hallucinate plausible-sounding but incorrect answers about satellite imagery content, a real risk for a tool meant to inform actual analysis decisions.

data_resource_availability.status: Public optical and SAR remote-sensing datasets exist for real training/testing.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: Not needed, real data access is achievable, though full multimodal combined datasets are less common than single-modality ones.

judge_qna.question: How do you ensure your model's answers are actually grounded in the real image, not hallucinated?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Describe your grounding approach (e.g. requiring the model to reference specific image regions/features) and demonstrate on a real image where you know the ground truth.
judge_qna.follow_up: What happens when your model is asked something the image genuinely doesn't show, does it admit uncertainty or fabricate an answer?

judge_qna.question: Did you achieve genuine optical-plus-SAR combined reasoning, or focus on one modality?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Be honest about your scope, if you focused on single-modality (optical) with strong multi-image reasoning as your core, explain that clearly and what full multimodal integration would additionally require.
judge_qna.follow_up: What's the biggest technical challenge in combining optical and SAR information for the same query?
